# Results -- Study 512 (High-Volume-Return-Premium) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: each Friday, rank a
40-name large-cap survivor basket by **abnormal volume** (this week's average daily volume /
its own trailing 8-week mean, minus 1); go long the top quintile (high volume), short the
bottom quintile (low volume), equal-weight, dollar-neutral; hold the forward week's return
(one execution lag -- enter the week **after** the signal is public). Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin
(2001). As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Daily simple returns | 3016 days × 40 tickers | `f8b840c95180` |
| Daily share volume | 3016 days × 40 tickers | `1235e9c48831` |
| Period covered | 2014-01-03 -- 2025-12-30 | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted close (returns) + raw `Volume` (signal), `auto_adjust=True`.
Universe: 40 current mega/large-cap US names. The panel is **survivorship-biased** -- current
large-caps projected backwards.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly, on the Signal axis):** only names still trading in 2026
are in the basket. A volume-spike sort is *especially* exposed to this -- blow-ups, takeovers and
delistings trade on enormous abnormal volume and are exactly the names removed from a survivor
basket. All results are **upper-bound** estimates; an opt-in guard would re-run on a
point-in-time membership list including delisted names.

## The honest test -- weekly high-volume / low-volume long-short

| Statistic (horizon = 1 week, **gross**) | Value |
|---|---|
| N weeks | 622 (2014 -- 2025) |
| Mean return (annualised) | **-5.47%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 14.08%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | -0.388 |
| **One-sample t** | **-1.343** |
| HAC (Newey-West) t | -1.328 |
| Hit rate (weeks > 0) | 49.2% |
| Max drawdown | -61.3% |

- The high-volume-minus-low-volume book earns **-5.47%/yr** at one-sample *t* = **-1.34** --
  the wrong sign for the GKM premium and well inside |*t*| < 2. On this modern mega-cap survivor
  tape the high-volume return premium **does not replicate**; if anything the high-volume
  quintile slightly *under*-performs the low-volume quintile.
- Leg detail: the high-volume (long) quintile earns **+19.47%/yr** forward, the low-volume
  (short) quintile **+24.94%/yr** -- both strongly positive in a bull sample, with the quiet
  names edging ahead.

## Label-shuffle placebo (is the sort real, or could random labels do as well?)

Permute the abnormal-volume labels across names *within each week* and recompute the mean
long-short, 200 times. The real mean sits comfortably inside the shuffled null.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Real mean (weekly) | -0.1051% |
| Null mean (weekly) | -0.0036% |
| Null std (weekly) | 0.0672% |
| **Placebo p-value** | **0.120** |
| Placebo p across base seeds (11 / 512 / 2026) | 0.125 / 0.100 / 0.117 |

The real long-short is **not** distinguishable from a random relabelling (p ≈ 0.12, stable
across seeds). The sort carries no information the labels themselves did not.

## Costs -- gross vs net

One-way **5 bps/leg** at formation (both legs trade each week; turnover is high), plus an annual
**50 bps** borrow on the low-volume short leg.

| Statistic | Gross | Net |
|---|--:|--:|
| Mean (annualised) | -5.47%/yr | **-11.17%/yr** |
| One-sample t | -1.343 | -2.743 |
| HAC t | -1.328 | -2.713 |
| Avg one-sided long-leg turnover | -- | 64.5%/week |

Costs make the (already negative) book *more* negative: the weekly quintile rebalance churns
~65% of the long basket every week, so 5 bps/leg compounds into a heavy drag. The net *t* of
-2.7 is "significant" only in the wrong direction -- there is no positive premium to harvest,
gross or net.

## Horizon robustness

| Horizon | Mean (ann) | One-sample t | Sharpe |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 week | -5.47% | -1.343 | -0.388 |
| 2 weeks | -9.15% | -1.613 | -0.467 |
| 4 weeks | -19.31% | -2.301 | -0.667 |
| 8 weeks | -33.06% | -2.703 | -0.786 |

Lengthening the horizon makes the (negative) drift *larger*, not smaller -- the opposite of the
GKM short-horizon-appreciation story. The high-volume quintile of modern large-caps persistently
trails the quiet quintile.

## Synthetic positive control (engine faithfulness -- NOT a real-tape claim)

Plant a known premium in a deterministic synthetic panel and confirm the engine recovers it
monotonically. This is a power check only; it is **never** cited for the real-tape verdict.

| Planted premium | Recovered LS mean (ann) | One-sample t |
|--:|--:|--:|
| -0.06 | -11.26% | -2.904 |
| -0.03 | -5.25% | -1.355 |
| 0.00 | +0.75% | +0.194 |
| +0.03 | +6.76% | +1.744 |
| +0.06 | +12.77% | +3.294 |
| +0.10 | +20.78% | +5.361 |

The engine is faithful: a planted premium of zero returns *t* ≈ 0.19 (a coin), and the recovered
long-short is monotone and significant in the planted premium. So the null result on the real
tape reflects **the market**, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** One-sample *t* = **-1.34** gross (HAC -1.33), the *wrong sign* for the
  GKM premium, and the label-shuffle placebo p = **0.12** (seed-robust) -- the sort is
  indistinguishable from random labels. The high-volume return premium does **not** survive on
  a 12-year modern large-cap survivor basket. None, not Weak: there is no positive effect here
  to even partially support, and the literature is for a far broader, older, less-watched NYSE
  universe (GKM 2001; Kaniel-Ozoguz-Starks 2012 note the premium is weakest where recognition
  frictions are smallest -- i.e. exactly these mega-caps).
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Gross Sharpe -0.39, net mean -11.17%/yr, ~65%/week turnover. Even
  if the sign had been right, weekly quintile churn at 5 bps/leg plus short borrow would bury it.
  There is nothing to trade.
- **Survivorship-biased? -- Named.** 40 current large-caps projected backwards; the failed and
  delisted names that trade on the biggest volume spikes are absent. Results are upper bounds --
  and the upper bound is already negative.
